source_text: i guess what i am thinking is that we would need hypergraphs for that "jumping back in" to work well.  the scopes in futon6 work are very rich.  i know we had done a previous llm backed mining round on operator turns that contributed to session-mode but that was a one off.  the scopes themselves are closer to intents than memories.

reply_text:
㊥ ("we would need hypergraphs") Agreed, and the store we already have is one: futon1b's memory edges are hyperedges, and the two things the move mining produces, an answer incidence and a scope, are hyperedges by nature, one paragraph bearing on several openers, one opener governing many later acts. I want to check what the futon6 scopes actually are before I say how close the analogy is.㊢ (recorded) Your remark is in the mission beside the first one (7bf772d0), with the consequence it has for the campaign now running.

㊣ ("we would need hypergraphs") Yes, and the two things the Zai mining produces are hyperedges by nature. An answer incidence is one reply paragraph bearing on several openers; a scope is one opener governing many later acts. Neither fits a binary edge, and both fit futon1b's hyperedge shape, which minus40 already uses for memory assertions and links. So the sidecars from the pilot are the mining output, not the carrier. The carrier is a `:xiang/answers` hyperedge over a paragraph and its openers, and a `:xiang/scope` hyperedge over an opener and what it governs, in the same store as the memories. That is what lets a resume brief traverse turns and memories as one graph.

㊬ (futon6 scopes, checked) Two things there, and they are both the right analogy. The thread hypergraph assembler types its nodes as post, term, expression and scope, and its hyperedges as mention, discourse, scope and so on, which is the same move: scope is a node kind with edges to what it governs. The LaTeX environment detector emits scope hyperedges from real structure, with a canonical kind table and an alias table, rather than matching prose headers, and it names the mistake that forced that: fake environments from bare "Lemma" lines. The dialogue equivalent is exactly what the pilot's validator enforces, a scope only where a verbatim act opens it.

㊟ ("closer to intents than memories") Agreed, and that settles where scopes live: on the 象 side, as acts' reach, in the kernel's vocabulary, not as facts in the memory store. A constraint in force, a focus declared, a mission named: each is an act whose scope is the set of later acts read under it. The kernel's standings are already half of this, the "in force until withdrawn" half; what they lack is the "governs these acts" relation, which is the hyperedge.

🈖 ("that was a one off") The earlier round mined operator turns into the 26 象 patterns and stopped. The difference this time is the output target: not patterns alone but a labelled grammar that a fast tier can apply to every settled turn afterwards, classical where the grammar is regular enough, Kimi where it is not. The Zai budget pays for the mining once; the standing cost is the fast tier. The pilot's numbers on precision and cost per record are what decide whether that is realistic, and they arrive on the next wake.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: ("continuing a familiar conversation") That is the test the whole inbox and memory work should be measured by, and it is better stated than anything in the spec, so I am recording your words verbatim in the mission and passing them to claude-15 as the memory-side aim. My read of how far the pieces reach, and the one gap, follows.㊢ (recorded) Your sentence is in the mission verbatim (f68aa393) and sent to claude-15 for the spec.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (what "familiar" would be made of) Picking up a conversation means knowing four things without rereading it: what is still owed and by whom, what rules and decisions are in force, what facts hold now and since when, and where it started. The first two are what today's record fields now give per session: open ports with their witnesses, standings in force or adopted-not-applied, obligations. The third is minus40's facts with referent dates. The fourth is the seed, which the missions already keep as operator-voice anchors. None of these needs a model to read.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (the gap) All of it is keyed by session, and a conversation is not a session. M-象-2000 ran through claude-14, claude-17, codex seats and now me, over three weeks, and nothing joins those sessions except the mission file. So "jumping in" today means reading the mission file, which is prose, not the four things above.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (the join exists; the artifact does not) Every agent-chat turn on the live store already carries its excursion and clocked target, and missions name their anchors. So a conversation can be defined classically as the turns across sessions that share a mission or excursion. The artifact is a resume brief per mission: its open ports, standings, obligations and recent facts, with the seed anchor at the top, read from record fields and the facts store and placed in the agent's first prompt. The scope grammar the Zai campaign mines would add the fifth thing, what we were working under when we stopped.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (how to know it worked) The measure I would fix before building: after a resume with the brief, does the agent's first turn re-ask or re-propose anything already settled in the brief? That is a count over real resumes, and it can fail.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (not started) You were thinking aloud, so nothing is dispatched for this beyond the record. The two parked jobs continue: codex-70's reload of the record fields and zai-1's labelling pilot.
